BreakupAnalysis.title: Breakup Analysis
BreakupAnalysis.helpBody: The Breakup Analysis plugin provides a database of major satellite breakup events in history. Select an event to view detailed information including the parent object, breakup cause, timeline from launch to breakup, and fragment dispersion analysis. The plugin searches the current catalog for tracked debris matching each event and displays statistical analysis of altitude ranges, eccentricity, and inclination distributions. Each event shows the international designator of the parent launch and the parent's NORAD number, so two events of the same rocket family (for example two CZ-6A upper stage breakups) cannot be confused.

fengyun1c.name: Fengyun-1C ASAT Test
fengyun1c.description: Chinese anti-satellite missile test that destroyed the Fengyun-1C weather satellite, creating the largest tracked debris cloud in history.

cosmos2251.name: Cosmos 2251 / Iridium 33 Collision
cosmos2251.description: First accidental hypervelocity collision between two intact satellites. Cosmos 2251 collided with the operational Iridium 33 communications satellite.

iridium33.name: Iridium 33 (from Collision)
iridium33.description: Debris field from the operational Iridium 33 satellite after collision with defunct Cosmos 2251.

cosmos1408.name: Cosmos 1408 ASAT Test
cosmos1408.description: Russian direct-ascent ASAT test that destroyed the defunct Cosmos 1408 ELINT satellite, generating debris that threatened the ISS crew.

microsatr.name: Microsat-R ASAT Test (Mission Shakti)
microsatr.description: Indian direct-ascent ASAT test (Mission Shakti) against the Microsat-R satellite. The low intercept altitude limited the long-lived debris population, though some fragments were lofted above the ISS.

breezem.name: Briz-M Upper Stage Explosion
breezem.description: Briz-M upper stage exploded after failed Arabsat-4A mission, likely due to residual propellant. Created debris across a wide range of altitudes.

cz6a.name: CZ-6A Upper Stage Breakup
cz6a.description: A Chinese Long March 6A second stage fragmented shortly after deploying Yunhai-3, scattering hundreds of fragments through heavily used sun-synchronous altitudes.

noaa16.name: NOAA-16 Breakup
noaa16.description: The decommissioned NOAA-16 weather satellite fragmented on orbit, attributed to a battery or thermal failure, adding long-lived debris to a congested polar altitude.

dmspf13.name: DMSP-F13 Breakup
dmspf13.description: A US Defense Meteorological Satellite Program spacecraft ruptured after a battery overcharge and overheating, a failure mode later traced across several DMSP and NOAA satellites of the same design.

usa193.name: USA-193 Shootdown
usa193.description: US Navy SM-3 missile destroyed the malfunctioning NRO satellite USA-193 (NROL-21). Low-altitude breakup meant most debris reentered within weeks.
